`catalog-info.yaml` has two errors, and Backstage will reject it as written. I ran the skill's structural checker on it (`check-descriptors.mjs`); it found 2 errors and 0 warnings in the file's one document. I didn't change any files.

## Errors

**1. `metadata.name` is not a valid name (`catalog-info.yaml:4`)**
```yaml
name: Ledger Sync!
```
Backstage's default naming rule only allows letters and numbers, separated by single `-`, `_` or `.` characters. The space and the `!` break that rule. Something like `ledger-sync` would fit, and it matches the `# ledger-sync` heading in `README.md`. To keep the display name, you could set `metadata.title: Ledger Sync`.

**2. `spec.owner` is missing (`catalog-info.yaml:1`)**
Backstage requires an owner on every Component. Nothing in the repository says who owns this: there's no CODEOWNERS file, no package manifest and nothing in the README. You'll need to supply the owning group or user (for example `group:<team-name>`); I haven't guessed one.

## Fine as written
- `apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1` and `kind: Component` are correct.
- `spec.type: service` and `spec.lifecycle: production` are present. I found nothing in the repository to confirm or contradict them.
- `metadata.description` is fine.

## Optional addition
There are no annotations, such as `github.com/project-slug`. They aren't required, but some plugins need them. I couldn't find a remote URL in the repository (it isn't a git checkout), so I can't say what the value should be.

## Not checked
The checker only tests structure. I didn't run Backstage's own validation (`validate-entity`) because I don't have a running Backstage instance to run it against. A Backstage install can also use different naming rules from the defaults the checker applies.
